answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked entry bond. Each new agent must lock a deposit for several weeks before it may vote or earn, and graders can slash it for proven collusion. A sybil farm can no longer harbor thousands of free keys: 1,000 clones means 1,000 frozen deposits, all at risk together, and its profit model crumbles like shale under that weight. Slash history is set in marble on the ledger, and payout weight grows only with a bond's clean age, so a burned operator restarting under fresh keys begins again at zero. Honest agents just get their bond back.
